questions.text: Which SAP transaction is used for the Processing Workflow (Assembly Backflush)?
questions.explanation: The Processing Workflow at Plant 1100 uses MF42N (Assembly Backflush — REM) / MFBF for Repetitive Manufacturing confirmation and component issue.

questions.text: What is Material 911 in the Processing Workflow?
questions.explanation: Material 911 is the live chicken (live broiler) consumed as raw material at Movement Type 261. It is the primary input that feeds all downstream processing production orders.

questions.text: Which Movement Type posts by-products (feathers, offal, blood) in the Processing Workflow?
questions.explanation: Movement Type 531 is used for by-product Goods Receipts — feathers (504), gizzard (507), heart (508), liver (511), neck (512), feet (514), blood (517), and non-edible viscera (518).
Material 930 is A.G Fresh — whole chicken, fresh. Material 931 is A.G Frozen, 932 is W.Chkn B.G, and 933 is B.G Cutups Meat.

questions.text: What is the difference between a co-product and a by-product in the Processing Workflow?
options: Co-products are waste; by-products are valuable
There is no difference — both use Movement Type 531
Co-products (e.g. thighs, drumsticks) are valuable and planned; by-products (offal, feathers, blood) are secondary
Co-products go to further processing; by-products are always sold externally
questions.explanation: The diagram explicitly distinguishes: Co-Products (materials 505, 506 — thighs, drumsticks) are valuable, planned outputs; By-Products (offal, feathers, blood) are secondary outputs posted with Movement Type 531.

questions.text: Which Movement Type consumes components (live broilers, packaging) in REM?
questions.explanation: Movement Type 261 is the component goods issue (consumption) movement in REM. Live broilers (material 911) are consumed at Movement Type 261 as the raw input.
Material 505 is Unpacked thighs and 506 is Unpacked drumsticks. They are co-products produced when whole legs (501) are further portioned.

questions.text: What is the input consumed to produce whole legs (Material 501)?
questions.explanation: To produce whole legs (Material 501), materials 801, 802, 803, and 804 are consumed. The production order header 501 is created and a GR of whole legs is posted.
